_comment: Shared vectors for issue #7681: which entity references
IfcRelDefinesByProperties.RelatingPropertyDefinition (attribute 5) names.
The attribute is an IfcPropertySetDefinitionSelect, so it is written as a
single ref, a bare set, or the typed IFCPROPERTYSETDEFINITIONSET((...)).
Rust half: rust/core/tests/property_definition_refs_parity.rs
(DecodedEntity::get_refs, via AttributeValue::as_ref_members).
TS half:   packages/parser/src/property-definition-refs.parity.test.ts
(readPropertyDefinitionRefs, extractPropertyRelFast and
propertyDefinitionRefsOfValue over the decoded attribute).
Each case is the attribute text. Both halves put it in slot 5 of
#1=IFCRELDEFINESBYPROPERTIES('g',$,$,$,(#50),<attr5>);
`refs` is the ids in written order, repeats kept, or null for no references
(get_refs -> None). `decodes: false` marks a record that does not tokenize:
Rust fails to decode it and TypeScript reads no references; both drop the
relationship. Only well-formed shapes are pinned: a lenient reading of a
malformed wrapper is deliberately not frozen here.
`decodedReader: false` skips the decoded-value reader for a case: the TS
EntityExtractor folds a typed value's arguments into ONE parsed value, so a
multi-argument wrapper is not the Rust `[name, a, b]` there. The byte readers
are the ones the parsers use and are always checked.

cases.name: non-reference members of a set are skipped
a string that looks like a reference is text
a nested list holds no direct reference
only the property set definition set is unwrapped
a wrapper must carry exactly one set argument
a set in a set is not unwrapped
